title: Do AI-based trading systems handle low liquidity situations differently in practice?
author: SlightYogurtcloset70
selftext:
One thing I have been thinking about with AI-driven trading systems is how they behave when liquidity is uneven. In traditional setups, low liquidity usually means delayed fills or less reliable pricing until more participants enter the market. I am wondering whether AI-based systems actually approach that differently in practice, especially in situations where the order book is thin or one-sided for a while.

Do they tend to wait for more data, adjust more aggressively, or does it usually end up producing more noise than useful structure? What has been your experience with AI trading systems in low liquidity conditions?
